definition: The four-verb formula describing the body's permeation by the quality generated in each of the four mental themes (jhana), used identically for each of the four in MN 39.
notes: The progression from drench to saturate to fill to spread shows thorough permeation without overflow: each verb intensifies the last rather than repeating it. Keep all four verbs in this order and this rendering wherever the mental-theme permeation formula recurs.

example_phrases.pali: so imameva kāyaṁ vivekajena pītisukhena abhisandeti parisandeti paripūreti parippharati
example_phrases.translation: they drench, saturate, fill, and spread this very body with the rejoicing and pleasure born of seclusion
example_phrases.notes: The first mental theme's permeation line; the same four verbs recur for the remaining three themes.
